items.title: Russia hits Ukraine's power grid again, leaving about 600,000 without electricity
items.summary: ABC News and CNN report that Russia fired ballistic missiles and drones at energy sites in Kyiv, the Kyiv region and Kharkiv overnight into 14 October, despite a US-announced 'energy ceasefire'. Zelensky says around 600,000 people lost power; Kyiv police reported five dead and 36 injured, while CBC counts at least nine killed across Ukraine. Casualty figures differ between outlets, so they are provisional.
items.why: Attacks on energy infrastructure move oil, gas and shipping costs worldwide, which feed into input prices for Indian firms and brands.

items.title: Saudi-led coalition reportedly intercepts Houthi missile aimed at Riyadh; crude edges higher
items.summary: A morning news recap dated 15 October says a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh was intercepted and that rising West Asia tension pushed crude oil prices up. This comes from a headline roundup rather than a full report, so details are provisional.
items.why: Gulf conflict keeps oil prices high, which squeezes consumer spending and company margins in India.

items.title: Jaishankar says India-US trade talks are nearing a 'landing point'
items.summary: Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said the two sides are working through key differences but gave no details and announced no breakthrough. Business Standard notes that Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman earlier called talks at a 'plateau' and the US trade representative said a deal is not imminent. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is due in Jamnagar and Mumbai from 17 to 22 October.
items.why: A trade deal decides tariffs on Indian exports, which shapes hiring and pricing in textiles, IT and consumer goods.

items.title: Police detain Ankita Bhandari's parents and Congress leaders at India Gate protest
items.summary: Latestly and Dynamite News report that Delhi Police detained the parents of Ankita Bhandari and opposition leaders during a sit-in at India Gate, and Congress accused the police of manhandling protesters. Coverage found was thin and from smaller outlets, so treat details as provisional.
items.why: Public protests and policing disputes shape political risk and brand reputation, a live case of crisis communication.

items.title: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is due to visit Jamnagar and Mumbai from 17 to 22 October
items.summary: Business Standard reports the visit as trade talks with the US near what India's foreign minister calls a 'landing point'.
items.why: A senior US visit during live trade talks signals how much weight both sides put on a deal.

items.title: Sensex slips 252 points to 72,782 as crude and inflation worries weigh
items.summary: Business Standard and Kotak Neo report that the Sensex closed 0.34% lower at 72,781.89 and the Nifty 0.44% lower at 22,622.70 on 14 October. They cite rising wholesale inflation, foreign investor outflows and crude near $107, while IT stocks held up and the pharma index fell about 1%.
items.why: Market swings track inflation and oil, which drive interest-rate expectations and corporate budgets, including marketing and hiring spend.

items.title: India's wholesale inflation jumps to 11.39% in September
items.summary: The Tribune and others report that WPI inflation rose to 11.39% in September from 9.92% in August, driven by mineral oils, food articles and crude petroleum and natural gas. Reports link the rise to the West Asia conflict and disruption around the Strait of Hormuz.
items.why: Higher input costs squeeze margins and often get passed on as price rises, a core pricing and brand-strategy issue.

items.title: WPI food inflation rose to 8.66% in September from 7.05% in August
items.summary: Reports on the 14 October Commerce Ministry release put food article inflation at 8.66%, up from 7.05% a month earlier.
items.why: Food prices hit household budgets first, which changes how FMCG shoppers trade down or switch brands.

items.title: Google lets US adults build personal Android apps with AI Studio, no developer account needed
items.summary: Archyde reports that a Google Play update in the US lets users aged 18 and older build personal Android apps in Google AI Studio without a developer account. It is dated 15 October and rests on a single secondary source, so treat it as provisional.
items.why: Lowering the barrier to building apps widens who can create tools, a platform-strategy move that matters for marketers and HR teams.

items.title: Meta releases Muse Wonder, its first frontier AI model
items.summary: TechCrunch reported on 12 October that Meta's Superintelligence Lab released Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, pitching 'Active Memory' for cross-conversation context and 'Active Focus' for goal persistence. Benchmark claims come from Meta and are unverified.
items.why: More strong model vendors change the build-versus-buy maths for HR and marketing teams adopting AI tools.
